[SHELL32] Implement CExtractIcon::Extract() (#9586)

This is needed for applications that use Java/Swing file open dialog.

- Before: https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/334a67d2-464e-4ec2-8722-3658a078a947
- After: https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/062b5252-1b6f-44af-b563-ced39d94d1d3

`CExtractIcon` is the shared `IExtractIcon` implementation returned by
`SHCreateDefaultExtractIcon()`, used by `CRegFolder`, `CFSFolder`,
`CDrivesFolder`, `CNetFolder`, `CControlPanelFolder` and `CPrinterFolder`.

Its `Extract()` method was a stub that returned `S_FALSE` without touching
the output icon handles. `S_FALSE` is the documented way to tell the caller
to load the icon itself from the location reported by `GetIconLocation()`,
but Windows performs the extraction here, and applications written against
Windows rely on that.

Applications that call `IExtractIcon::Extract()` directly therefore
got no icon at all like NetBeans that uses Java/Swing file open dialog,
which asks the shell folder for `IID_IExtractIconW`, calls `Extract()`,
and falls back to a generic icon when the returned handle is NULL.

The result is that My Computer, My Documents and My Network Places
are drawn as blank document icons.
ReactOS shell itself was unaffected because `PidlToSicIndex()` only calls
`GetIconLocation()` and loads the icon through the shell icon cache,
so it never exercised `Extract()`.

- `CExtractIcon::Extract()` now extracts the icon with `SHDefExtractIconW()`.
  Failures still return `S_FALSE`, so callers that extract by location
  keep working as before.
- `SHDefExtractIconW()`: zero-initialize `hIcons[2]`.
- When the caller passes a NULL `phiconSmall` and `PrivateExtractIconsW()`
  returned only one icon, the function called `DestroyIcon()`
  on an uninitialized handle.

Note that it uncovers some problems with `user32::PrivateExtractIconsW`,
which could extract wrong icon sizes, see CORE-9533 and CORE-20060.
